topics.label: Course conclusion and lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives on cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms, applications, systemic toxicities, and resistance pathways associated with traditional surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor vulnerabilities and checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies that take advantage of cancer-specific vulnerabilities in hormone dependency, cell cycle checkpoint regulation, and DNA damage repair.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the rationale of targeting oncogene-addicted kinases and the structural and pathway alterations that lead to drug resistance.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the engineering and clinical use of antibody formats to target cell surface antigens and deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the evidence for natural immune surveillance and cover therapeutic strategies that activate or engineer immune cells against tumors.

topics.label: Broader challenges, historical progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical mortality trends, current clinical hurdles, and evolving paradigms in cancer management.
